newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BA unworried by EU on American deal.
newsitem.headline: BA unworried by EU on American deal.

text.p: British Airways (BA) Plc Chairman Sir Colin Marshall said on Monday he was not worried by any possibility that the European Union would block BA's plan to form an alliance with AMR Corp's American Airlines.
"I'm not worried about it because I don't think that that is likely to happen," Marshall told reporters in Sydney after a luncheon address.
"There are so many precedents for similar events that have been allowed to go into effect, that to me it would be quite wrong if the European Union reached that conclusion," he said.
"So I think that it is most unlikely that they would and I'm not unduly concerned," he said.
On Friday, the European Commission said it had formally asked BA for details of the planned alliance.
A report that the EC had said the alliance did not appear to be in the best interests of consumers pushed BA's shares lower earlier on Friday.
Marshall said BA was awaiting the approval of the British government, before seeking the approval of the U.S. Department of Transportation.
"That will obviously take quite a lot longer to achieve, particularly given the fact that the Secretary of Transportation has resigned and one I suppose will be waiting for a new secretary," he said.

The British and U.S. governments were in the meantime in talks on the bilateral issue of "open skies" between the two, a precondition set by the U.S. government for the BA/American alliance to go ahead.
"I think things are all moving in the right direction, but it's just very slow," Marshall said. REUTER
